name: Hagar
description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: and she had an handmaid, an Egyptian, whose name was Hagar: so remember, it said he had a son by a bondmaid. Hagar was a handmaid to his wife.
Hagar was Sarai's Egyptian handmaid, from the servants Pharaoh gave in Genesis 12:16.
took Hagar her maid the Egyptian: her maid, her bondmaid.
Sarai laid the wrong on Abram, and Abram answered, Behold, thy maid is in thy hand. He did not say my wife; he had no attachment to Hagar. His sole purpose was the seed, not multiple wives.
And he went in unto Hagar: he did what? He went in unto Hagar.
When Hagar conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes. Hagar got high minded; she stopped submitting because she carried Abram's child.
when Hagar bare Ishmael to Abram: right? So now Abraham had a son by Hagar. His name was Ishmael. That's the bondmaid son.

Abram was fourscore and six years old, eighty six, when Hagar bare Ishmael. Ishmael was Abram's firstborn, but the covenant did not go to Ishmael; the covenant goes through the twelve tribes of Israel.

Abraham rose up early, took bread and a bottle of water, gave it to Hagar, and sent her away with the child. That is important, because the Arabs love to talk about Abraham, we are descendants of Abraham, the Abrahamic religions. Abraham gave you a bottle of water and some bread and sent you away.

note.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: Tell me, ye that desire to be under the law, the sacrifice of the weak and beggarly elements, do ye not hear the law? Abraham had two sons, one by a bondmaid, Hagar, born after the flesh, Ishmael, and one by a freewoman, Sarah, by promise. Which things are an allegory, for these are the two covenants: Hagar is the old, from mount Sinai, which gendereth to bondage, bound to offering up animals; Sarah is the new.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: Which things are an allegory: so now, which goes back to the topic of the lesson. These things, that history, everything that happened in Genesis that we read in chapter 16, chapter 17, Hagar having Ishmael and the Lord promising Sarah to have Isaac, that was an allegory.

This Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia, and answereth to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children under temple law. But Jerusalem which is above is free, because Christ died, and is the mother of us all. Rejoice, thou barren that bearest not: Sarah.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: For this Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia: so now it says this Agar, this old covenant, is Mount Sinai in Arabia. Well, Mount Sinai itself, where we went to get the law, statutes, and commandments, including the sacrificial law, is not in the land of Arabia. So why is it saying this Agar is Mount Sinai in Arabia? Mount Sinai is not in the land of Arabia geographically. But watch this.

For this Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia: meaning what? You have certain Israelites living in Arabia, scattered like Deuteronomy 4:27 says, still keeping the old covenant of sacrificial law, those continual burnt offerings. They were still doing those things in Arabia.
For this Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia: right? You had Israelites that still kept the covenant of animal sacrifice, living in Arabia.
